course_name_original: Liberalisierung und Regulierung in der Energiewirtschaft
course_name_en: Liberalisation and Regulation in Power Economics

learning_outcomes.text: Students have a basic understanding of the distinction between liberalized and regulated parts of pipeline-bound energy transport. They know the basic idea of capital cost accounting and the distinction between total capital interest and the breakdown into debt and equity interest.

Students have a basic understanding of exchange and over-the-counter energy trading and the handling of physical deviations in generation and consumption with the help of balancing groups. They have also understood the basic principles of setting network charges and incentive regulation.

Students know the technical terms common in the liberalized (especially exchange-based) and regulated (especially renewable energies) energy markets and their meaning. The same applies to the regulation of energy network charges.
Students can perform simple profitability calculations (present value method, annuitization of one-off amounts) and know the basic determination of a notional interest rate using the CAPM method.
Students can fundamentally understand, classify, and explain changes in behavior of electricity market participants and network operators in response to changes in the legal or regulatory framework.

syllabus_topics: Legal basis for liberalization and regulation in the EU and Germany
Explanation of the unbundled market model
Excursion: Analogies in electricity and gas industry
assessment_rules: The graded examination performance can be either a term paper or an oral examination. The form of examination will be agreed upon at the beginning of the semester, with the term paper being the standard case. The term paper should be 10-20 pages, with an explanation of approx. 20 minutes if applicable. The duration of the oral examination is as per the general part of the examination regulations.
bibliography: Topic-specific literature search during the course
